name: pgEdge
tagline: Fully open-source multi-master distributed PostgreSQL built on the Spock logical replication extension.
description: pgEdge packages standard PostgreSQL with Spock, its multi-master logical replication extension, plus Snowflake sequences and large-object replication, to run active-active Postgres clusters across regions or edge sites. Each node is a normal Postgres server accepting writes, and Spock replicates changes asynchronously with configurable conflict resolution and delta-apply for counters. In September 2025 pgEdge relicensed all components under the PostgreSQL License, and it sells Enterprise Postgres builds, support and a managed offering. It suits globally distributed apps that can tolerate eventual consistency between nodes, not workloads needing distributed serializable transactions.

pricing.notes: All components open source; paid support, Enterprise Postgres builds and managed cloud.

scale.notes: Full copies on each node with async multi-master replication; no automatic sharding.

strengths: Active-active writes in every region using standard PostgreSQL
Conflict resolution and delta-apply columns for counters
Runs on any cloud or on-prem, including air-gapped sites
weaknesses: Asynchronous replication means conflicts and eventual consistency between nodes
No automatic sharding: every node holds all data
Schema and sequence design must account for multi-master
Smaller vendor and community than mainstream Postgres distributions
useCases: Multi-region active-active applications with low local latency
Edge deployments that must keep writing during network partitions
Zero-downtime major-version upgrades via logical replication
Data residency setups with regional write nodes
notIdealFor: Datasets too large to replicate fully to every node
Teams wanting a single-region primary-replica setup
